John holds WOLDINGHAM from Richard. Wulfstan held it from King Edward. Then it answered for 8 hides, now for 1. Land [for *** ploughs]. In lordship 1 1/2 ploughs; 6 villagers and 3 smallholders with 3 ploughs. 3 slaves.
notes: Great Domesday seldom counts livestock outside the south-west, so no flocks are drawn unless the entry gives them.

12767.tic: Richard son of Count Gilbert/of Clare/of Tonbridge
q: Surrey 19,16

Richard holds WOODMANSTERNE himself, in lordship. Azur held it from King Edward. Then and now it answered for 15 hides, but it never paid tax. Land for 3 ploughs. In lordship 2 ploughs; 1 villager and 12 cottagers with 3 ploughs.
notes: Great Domesday seldom counts livestock outside the south-west, so no flocks are drawn unless the entry gives them.

q: Surrey 18,3

Turold [nephew of Wigot] holds WORPLESDON from the Earl. Osmund held it from King Edward. Then it answered for 8 hides, now for 6 1/2 hides. Land for 7 ploughs. In lordship 1 plough; 13 villagers and 3 smallholders with 6 ploughs.
notes: Great Domesday seldom counts livestock outside the south-west, so no flocks are drawn unless the entry gives them.

q: Surrey 36,4

In WOTTON Hundred Oswald [brother of Abbot Wulfwold] holds WOTTON himself. [Earl] Harold held it before 1066, but the men of the Hundred state that they do not know how Harold had it. Then it answered for 6 hides, now for 5 hides.
notes: Great Domesday seldom counts livestock outside the south-west, so no flocks are drawn unless the entry gives them.
